title_en: Chongqing Yutian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd., Chongqing Branch — dispute over joint construction of housing
ruling_gist_en: 1. Where the two agreements reached by the parties on the basis of equality and voluntariness are in compliance with the law and are legal and valid, the contents agreed upon in both agreements shall be binding on the parties. When both contracts (agreements) are valid contracts (agreements), and unless the parties have otherwise agreed, if the earlier and later contracts (agreements) have conflicting provisions on the same matter, based on the most recent expression of intent and provided that it does not violate the purpose of the contract (agreement), the content determined by the later contract (agreement) shall prevail in accordance with the chronological order of formation of the contracts (agreements). If the contents agreed upon in the earlier and later contracts (agreements) are not in conflict, but merely contain different stipulations on the content of the contract (agreement), it cannot be simply determined that the later agreement is an amendment to the earlier agreement, or that the later agreement is a supplementation and perfection of the earlier agreement.
keywords_en: Civil; housing joint construction dispute; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Chongqing Municipality; legal person; Contract Law; determination of validity when successive agreements conflict; principle of party disposition and principle of no trial without complaint; reversal of judgment; joint housing construction; investment distribution; delivery of houses; autonomy of will; no trial without complaint; Chongqing Branch housing joint construction dispute
full_text_en:
Chongqing Yutian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Chongqing Branch, Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd. — dispute over joint building of houses

【Ruling Summary】

I. Where two agreements are reached by the parties on the basis of equality and voluntariness, both conform to legal provisions, are legally valid, and the contents stipulated in both agreements shall be binding on the parties. When both contracts (agreements) are valid, unless the parties have otherwise agreed, if the two successive contracts (agreements) contain conflicting provisions on the same matter, based on the principle that the most recent expression of intent prevails, and provided that the contract (agreement) purpose is not violated, the content of the later contract (agreement) shall prevail as determined by the chronological order of the contracts (agreements). If the provisions of the two successive contracts (agreements) do not conflict but merely stipulate different content, it cannot be simply concluded that the later agreement is an amendment to, or a supplement or improvement of, the prior agreement.

II. The principle that parties may dispose of their civil and litigation rights within the scope prescribed by law, and the principle of "no trial without complaint," are important principles in civil litigation. When a people's court handles civil and commercial disputes, it may only make determinations on the civil rights and obligations that have been submitted to the court. Except when involving state or public interests, its trial and judgment shall be limited to the scope of the requests and claims of the parties.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2011) Min Kang Zi No. 48

Protesting authority: Supreme People's Procuratorate of the People's Republic of China.

Appellant (defendant at first instance, appellant at second instance): Chongqing Branch, Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 103 Xinhua Road, Yuzhong District, Chongqing.

Responsible person: Feng Jianlong, Branch Manager.

Agent ad litem: Chen Li, female, Han nationality, born on July 16, 1976, residing at Room 9-2, Building 3, No. 47 Xiaolongkan New Street, Shapingba District, Chongqing, an employee of this Branch.

Appellee (plaintiff at first instance, appellee at second instance): Chongqing Yutian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 177 Bayi Road, Yuzhong District, Chongqing.

Legal representative: Lei Ming, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

In the case of dispute over joint building of houses between the appellant, Chongqing Branch, Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch), and the appellee, Chongqing Yutian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yutian Company), the appellant was dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2001) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 118 rendered by the Chongqing High People's Court and appealed to the procuratorial authority. The Supreme People's Procuratorate filed a protest with this Court by means of Civil Protest Letter Gao Jian Min Kang [2011] No. 9. This Court rendered a civil ruling (2011) Min Kang Zi No. 48 on June 17, 2011, to retry the case, and formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing. The Supreme People's Procuratorate designated Procurator Tian Li and Clerk Wang Liuyu to appear in court and read the protest letter. Chen Li, the agent ad litem of the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch, and Lei Ming, the legal representative of Yutian Company, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

The facts found by this court upon retrial are as follows:

On January 8, 1996, Yutian Company (Party A) and the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch (Party B) entered into the "General Agreement on Joint Building of Houses," Article 1 of which, concerning the form of joint building, provided: 1. Party A shall be responsible for the entire implementation of the Yutian Building Project and shall decide on all major matters concerning the project's operation; 2. Party B shall participate in the joint building of houses with Party A by way of investment and shall share in the distribution of housing units. Article 2, concerning joint operation and obligations, provided: 1. Party A shall be responsible for the preliminary work of the entire project and for completing the relevant procedures, including planning, land use, fire control, environmental sanitation, and municipal administration. 2. Party A shall be responsible for the demolition, relocation, and civil engineering construction of the entire project. 3. Party B shall ensure that funds are available in a timely manner to facilitate the smooth progress of the project. Article 3, concerning engineering standards, provided: 1. The exterior of the building shall be an aluminum alloy glass curtain wall, using imported Belgian glass and American Reynolds aluminum panels; 2. The flooring shall be granite flooring (Luding Sesame White); 3. Equipment: A. Three American Otis elevators, Model 411; B. Fourteen Suzhou Schindler SDS escalators; C. The central air-conditioning system shall be American York brand water-cooled screw chillers; D. The fire alarm equipment shall be Japanese "Nittan" alarm devices; 4. Public facilities: shall be delivered and put into use within two months after delivery of the housing units; public facilities include: A. Power supply; B. Water supply; C. Communications; D. Fire control; E. Environmental protection; F. Demolition and clearance of temporary transitional houses, leveling of sidewalks, and implementation of greening and light enhancement projects; G. Other public facilities shall be completed by Party A. 5. If Party B requests changes to the above facilities and equipment, such changes shall be handled after obtaining Party A's consent, and the increased investment shall be added or deducted proportionately from the joint investment. Article 4, concerning investment methods and distribution, provided: 1. Party B shall participate in the joint building of houses by way of investment and shall receive housing units after the building is completed; 2. The parties have agreed through negotiation that Party B shall receive the first basement floor commercial premises by way of investment, and the final accounting shall be based on the area of the industrial property recognized by both parties; 3. Party B shall invest a total of RMB 57,000,000 in cash to Party A for the joint building of houses (final accounting based on the actual industrial property area); 4. Party B shall participate in joint building by way of investment and shall receive the first basement floor commercial premises after completion; through negotiation, the parties have agreed that the first basement floor commercial premises shall be accounted for in two parts: Part one: Party B's subordinate Business Department shall invest RMB 20,000,000 and receive 1,000 square meters of floor area in the first basement floor commercial premises. Part two: For the remaining part of the first basement floor commercial premises (including 1,598 square meters of commercial space and 398.53 square meters of public area apportionment in the building), 80% of the investment amount of RMB 37,000,000 shall be paid upon delivery for use, 15% upon transfer of property title, and the remaining balance shall be settled upon expiration of the warranty period. If Party B's investment is not made in a timely manner, the resulting interest shall be borne by Party B. 5. To ensure the smooth completion of the joint building project, Party B shall coordinate multiple channels for loans and introduce funds to support the project construction; such loans shall bear interest at the standard rate prescribed by the state at that time; the amount of loans coordinated and funds introduced shall not be less than the investment amount of the second part. Article 5, concerning matters related to handover of housing units, provided: 1. Party A shall hand over the housing units to Party B no later than July 1997, after ensuring the completion of the public facilities specified in Article 3(4), for Party B to carry out finishing decoration; Party A shall cooperate. Party B's decoration shall not damage the structure, public facilities, or common areas, and shall comply with Party A's overall arrangements during the decoration period; 2. Party A shall handle the property title registration for the housing units distributed to Party B. Taxes and fees incurred in the registration of property title shall be borne by each party in the amounts for which they are respectively liable; 3. After Party B enters the building, it shall comply with the unified property management of the entire building and abide by the relevant regulations of the building; security for the first basement floor commercial premises shall be the responsibility of Party B. Article 6, concerning liability for breach of contract, provided: 1. If either Party A or Party B withdraws in breach of contract, it shall pay liquidated damages in the amount of 5% of the total investment amount; 2. If Party B's investment amount is not made in a timely manner as agreed, it shall pay a late payment penalty of 0.01% per day on the shortfall; 3. If Party A fails to deliver the housing units to Party B on time, it shall pay a late delivery penalty of 0.01% per day on the total investment amount. Article 7, concerning other matters, provided: Matters not covered in the agreement shall be resolved through separate negotiation; any supplementary agreements signed shall have the same legal effect.

On January 20, 1996, Yutian Company (Party A) and the Business Department of Chongqing Branch, Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch Business Department, Party B) entered into the "Joint Building of Houses Agreement," Article 3 of which, concerning investment and distribution, provided: 1. Party B shall invest a total of RMB 20,000,000 in Party A for joint building of houses and shall receive 1,000 square meters in the first basement floor of the building; 2. When the building reaches the eighth floor, Party B shall have paid the full cash investment and shall supervise its use; 3. Through negotiation, the parties have agreed that the following items are included in the distribution: A. The foyer of the main entrance of the building shall be used by Party B to display the signage "Agricultural Bank of China" in large characters; B. One side of the roof of the main building facing Linjiangmen and the roof of the podium building, with a width of 30 meters, shall be provided to Party B free of charge for use as advertising space; C. The housing units distributed to Party B shall be equipped with individual electric meters; in the future, Party B shall pay for electricity based on its meter readings and shall not participate in the building's shared electricity costs. Water and cooling fees shall be apportioned on a pro rata basis. D. When the housing units are distributed, Party B shall have the right to choose its location within the first basement floor on a priority basis. Article 4, concerning matters related to handover of housing units, provided: Party A shall hand over the housing units to Party B for use no later than July 30, 1997. The other provisions were generally consistent with those in the "General Agreement on Joint Building of Houses."

On March 16, 1996, Yutian Company (Party A) and the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch Business Department (Party B) entered into a "Joint Building of Houses Agreement," providing: Party A and Party B's subordinate Business Department signed the "Joint Building of Houses Agreement" on January 20, 1996. Now, through friendly negotiation between Party A and Party B, Party B has decided, on the basis of the January 20, 1996 "Joint Building of Houses Agreement," to continue to participate in Party A's construction of the Yutian Building by way of investment. Article 3, concerning investment and distribution, provided: 1. Party B shall invest a total of RMB 37,000,000 in Party A to participate in the joint building of houses and shall receive 1,996.53 square meters in the first basement floor of the building (including 1,598 square meters of commercial space, calculated at RMB 21,650 per square meter, and 398.53 square meters of public area apportionment in the building, calculated at RMB 4,500 per square meter); 2. The investment method is: when Party A distributes the housing units to Party B, Party B shall pay 80% of the RMB 37,000,000 to Party A; when the property title is transferred to Party B, Party B shall pay an additional 15% of the total; the remaining balance shall be paid upon expiration of the warranty period. Article 4, concerning matters related to handover of housing units, provided: Party A shall hand over the housing units to Party B for use no later than July 30, 1997. Additionally, except for the provisions "If the investment of the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch is not made in a timely manner, the resulting interest shall be borne by the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch" and "To ensure the smooth completion of the joint building project, the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch shall coordinate multiple channels for loans and introduce funds for the project construction; such loans shall bear interest at the standard rate prescribed by the state at that time. The amount of loans coordinated and funds introduced shall not be less than the investment amount of the second part," which were not recorded, the other provisions were generally consistent with those in the "General Agreement on Joint Building of Houses."

On December 28, 1995, construction of the Yutian Building commenced. On July 12, 1996, the Yutian Building obtained project approval No. (1996) 462 from the Chongqing Municipal Planning Commission under the Chongqing Municipal Heavy Commission Fixed Assets [1996] No. 462, with a construction scale of 46,810 square meters. On September 2, 1996, Yutian Company obtained the State-Owned Land Use Certificate for the Yutian Building, Yu Guo Yong (1996) Zi No. 053.

The "Structural Acceptance Record" dated December 7, 1996, stated: Project name: Yutian Building; Structural type, number of floors: frame-shear wall structure, 29 floors; Acceptance location: foundation structure; Building area: 51,000 square meters; Relevant content was inspected; the item "existing quality hazards" was crossed out; the quality assurance materials were checked, with the conclusion being "meets requirements" or "pass"; the "Conclusion" column was left blank; representatives of the four parties, including the quality supervision station, design unit, construction unit (or supervision unit), and construction unit, signed in the corresponding columns, but none affixed the official seal of their respective units. The "Structural Engineering Acceptance Record" dated April 17, 1997, stated: Construction date: December 28, 1995; Acceptance date: April 14, 1997; Other contents were the same as the December 7, 1996 "Structural Acceptance Record"; the "Acceptance Conclusion" column was left blank. Representatives of the four parties, including the quality supervision station, design, construction (or supervision), and construction units, signed in the corresponding columns, but none affixed the official seal of their respective units.

On May 13, 1997, the Yutian Building obtained the "Commercial Housing Pre-Sale (Pre-Lease) Permit" No. Chong Fang 97 Yu Zi No. 0039, which stated: Project completion time: September 1998; Valid period: December 1998; On May 8, 2000, the Chongqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Housing agreed to extend the validity period of the "Commercial Housing Pre-Sale (Pre-Lease) Permit" for the Yutian Building to the end of October 2000.

The "Interim Acceptance Record" dated October 28, 1997, stated: Project name: Yutian Building; Handover inspection location: -4.45 floor, first basement floor, and fire control center; Start date: December 28, 1995; Interim delivery date: October 28, 1997. Interim handover inspection items included frame-shear wall structure main body, wooden doors, fire doors, ceiling sprinklers, fire hydrant boxes, smoke detectors, etc.; the inspection and handover opinion was "Passed acceptance, meeting use conditions, agreed to hand over to the next process of finishing decoration"; representatives of the quality supervision station, design unit, receiving party, and handing-over party all signed and affixed the official seals of their respective units; the fire protection department did not affix its seal.

On December 17, 1997, Yutian Company and the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch Business Department completed the handover procedures for the housing units and signed the "Handover and Use Approval Form" (hereinafter referred to as the "Approval Form"), which stated: Project name: Yutian Building; Project item: Agricultural Bank business hall; Floor: First basement floor, axes 9-J-11; The portion belonging to the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch was the first basement floor, axes 1-9. Yutian Company, as the construction unit handing over, and the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch Business Department, as the owner, affixed their seals on the Approval Form to confirm. The Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch Business Department also paid the purchase price in full as agreed.

On October 19, 1998, Yutian Company sent a letter to the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch stating: "Your branch signed a house purchase agreement with our company on January 8, 1996. The house construction is now completed. Please perform the agreement and take delivery of the housing units before the 23rd of this month, and deduct the outstanding purchase price of RMB 37,000,000 from our company's loans at your branch. From October 23 onward, our company will no longer bear the interest on the RMB 37,000,000 purchase price. Additionally, please support our company's loan application as per Article 4(5) of the agreement." The Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch did not take delivery of the housing units or make payment. On May 5, 1999, Yutian Company sent a "Letter Urging the Agricultural Bank to Pay for Joint Building of Houses" to the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch, stating: "Our company and your branch signed the 'Joint Building of Houses Agreement' in January 1996 and received part of the joint building payment of RMB 20,000,000 from your branch in December 1996. The remaining joint building payment should have been paid to our company in July 1996 according to the agreement. Our company has delivered the housing units to your branch in December 1997 and has issued multiple notices, but your branch has not yet responded. Currently, the project still has finishing work pending. Due to lack of funds, the project has been shut down for some time, causing our company to be unable to pay loan interest or engineering funds, resulting in huge losses, with losses of more than one hundred thousand yuan every day. We hope that your branch will promptly study and pay the joint building payment. If there is still no response, it may affect the bank-enterprise relationship, and our company will have no choice but to resort to legal action." On July 19, 2000, Yutian Company sent a "Notice Urging the Agricultural Bank to Pay for Joint Building of Houses" to the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch, stating: "Your branch and our company signed the 'Joint Building of Houses Agreement' in January 1996. Our company delivered the housing units to your branch in 1997 as agreed, but your branch has delayed paying the construction payment of RMB 37,000,000 to our company. We hereby notify you again to pay the housing payment to our company."

On November 8, 2000, the Chongqing Municipal Construction Engineering Quality Supervision Station issued a certificate stating: "The main structure of the Yutian Building developed and constructed by Chongqing Yutian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. has been inspected by both Party A and Party B, the design unit, and the quality supervision station, and the quality has reached the acceptance standard."

Separately found: On May 24, 2000, Yutian Company and Sichuan McDonald's Restaurant Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as McDonald's Company) entered into a "McDonald's House Lease Contract," leasing 782 square meters of the street-facing portion of the building on the first basement floor, axes 1-9, to McDonald's Company for a lease term starting from the restaurant's opening date and continuing until 15 full years of operation. McDonald's Company shall pay rent to Yutian Company each month starting from the rental commencement date, calculated as 5% of the monthly after-tax sales revenue.

On August 8, 2000, Yutian Company filed a lawsuit with the Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, requesting: 1. An order that the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch immediately pay the first installment of the joint building construction payment in the amount of RMB 29,600,000; 2. That the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch bear the interest on the overdue payment (calculated from July 30, 1997, to August 2000, a total of 39 months) in the amount of RMB 7,272,720; 3. That the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch bear the late payment penalty on the unpaid purchase price (calculated from July 30, 1997, to August 2000, a total of 39 months) at 0.01% per day, totaling RMB 3,463,200; 4. That the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch bear all litigation costs in this case. On June 22, 2001, the Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2000) Yu Yi Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 1696. Yutian Company, dissatisfied, filed an appeal on July 3, 2001, requesting that the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch not only pay the purchase price as ordered in the first instance judgment but also bear the interest and liquidated damages for the funds that were not made available in a timely manner as agreed, including interest on the funds not made available in a timely manner (from November 1997 to July 2001) in the amount of RMB 11,034,471.72; and that the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch bear all litigation costs. During the inquiry by the court of second instance on November 12, 2001, with Lei Ming, the legal representative of Yutian Company, Lei Ming expressly requested that the late payment penalty and interest be calculated up to the date of enforcement. In its appeal, the Agricultural Bank Chongqing Branch argued that the court of first instance had failed to hold Yutian Company liable for the late delivery penalty (calculated at 0.01% per day) for delivering the housing units more than three years after the agreed delivery date, which was manifestly unfair.

Separately found: On February 25, 2003, the Chongqing Municipal Public Security Bureau Fire Department issued the "Opinion on Fire Acceptance Inspection of Yutian Building" Yu Gong Xiao Yan Zi (2003) No. 4119, stating: "The Yutian Building (located in Jiefangbei, with acceptance scope of floors 9 to 26 and the first basement floor, classified as a Class I public building) declared by Yutian Company has undergone a fire acceptance inspection. It is hereby determined that the fire acceptance inspection of this project is qualified."

Separately found: On November 26, 2001, the Chongqing High People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2001) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 118, and on December 10 of the same year, issued the civil ruling (2001) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 118, correcting a clerical error in the said judgment, specifically "changing the total investment amount of RMB 36,000,000 in the first line on page 15 to RMB 37,000,000." The contents of the said judgment were fully performed on December 10, 2001.

In August 2003, the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China filed a lawsuit with the Chongqing High People's Court, requesting that Yutian Company designate the location of the building's basement floor premises, deliver the premises, and handle the property rights registration. The Chongqing High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment No. 14 (2003) Yu Gao Fa Min Chu Zi, holding that: (1) Yutian Company shall, immediately upon the effectiveness of this judgment, deliver to the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China the property rights to the 1,903.83 square meters within axes 1-9 on the basement floor of the building and complete the property rights registration procedures; (2) Yutian Company shall compensate the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China for interest losses on RMB 29,600,000 (calculated in installments based on the People's Bank of China's loan interest rate for the corresponding period, from January 1, 2002, until the date of delivery of the property ownership certificate); (3) All other claims of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China were dismissed. Both Yutian Company and the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China appealed to the Supreme People's Court. On June 17, 2004, the Supreme People's Court issued Civil Judgment No. 8 (2004) Min Yi Zhong Zi, holding that: (1) Item (1) of Civil Judgment No. 14 (2003) Yu Gao Fa Min Chu Zi of the Chongqing High People's Court was affirmed; (2) Items (2) and (3) of Civil Judgment No. 14 (2003) Yu Gao Fa Min Chu Zi of the Chongqing High People's Court were reversed; (3) Yutian Company shall pay to the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China rent for the 1,996.53 square meters of premises, calculated at a standard rate of RMB 140 per square meter per month (from December 11, 2001, until the actual date of delivery of the premises); (4) All other claims of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China were dismissed.

Further findings: Pursuant to the Reply of the China Banking Regulatory Commission on the Restructuring of the Agricultural Bank of China into a Joint-Stock Company, Yin Jian Fu [2009] No. 13, the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China changed its name to the Chongqing Branch of Agricultural Bank of China Limited.

The First Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing held at first instance that: 1. The "Joint Building Agreement" signed by both parties on March 16, 1996, was a contract in the name of joint building but in substance a purchase agreement. This contract reflected the true intent of both parties, did not violate legal provisions, and should be valid. Because the "General Joint Building Agreement" signed on January 6, 1996, explicitly specified the allocation of premises and that the investment amount included the portion allocated to the Business Department of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China. Subsequently, the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China and its Business Department separately entered into new "Joint Building Agreements" with Yutian Company regarding their respective investment allocations. These two later agreements constituted an amendment to the earlier "General Joint Building Agreement," and since the subject matter of Yutian Company's lawsuit was limited to the portion invested by the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, the disputed facts in this case should be governed by the "Joint Building Agreement" signed by the parties on March 16, 1996. Examining the content of this agreement, the method of allocating premises differs from typical joint building arrangements. In typical joint building, the allocation is directly based on axes or floors, whereas the allocation method agreed upon by the parties involved calculating the price of the allocated area at RMB 21,650 per square meter, plus a method for settling common area apportionment at RMB 4,500 per square meter. The payment of the investment was not due upon signing the contract, but rather upon Yutian Company's completion of the building and delivery to the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, at which time the first installment of investment, i.e., 80% of RMB 37,000,000, would be paid. Yutian Company was responsible for handling the property rights formalities for the delivered premises, and the transfer of title was made a condition for the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China to pay the second installment of the investment. The liquidated damages clause provided that if Yutian Company delayed delivery of the premises, it would pay a late fee of 0.1‰ per day of the total investment amount, and if the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China delayed payment of the investment, it would also pay a late fee of 0.1‰ per day of the shortfall. From the above content, this agreement more closely resembles the external characteristics of a purchase contract, therefore this agreement is in name a joint building agreement but in substance a real estate purchase. Regarding the content stipulated in the agreement, it does not violate the provisions of laws and regulations. Although at the time Yutian Company signed the agreement with the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, it had not yet obtained the State-owned Land Use Certificate and the Commercial Housing Pre-sale (Pre-lease) Permit for Yutian Building, Yutian Company later obtained both documents. Pursuant to Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (I) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 51 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, this agreement shall be deemed valid. Although both parties engaged in conduct to circumvent the law, this did not cause loss to the State and does not affect the validity of the contract. The defense of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China that the joint building agreement should be invalid for failure to go through joint building procedures, or that even if it is in name a joint building but in substance a sale it should be invalid, cannot be sustained. 2. The premises that Yutian Company intended to deliver met the conditions for delivery. Since the agreement signed by both parties is valid, both parties should perform their respective obligations in accordance with the agreement. As long as the premises Yutian Company intended to deliver met the conditions for delivery, the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China should have accepted the premises and paid the first installment of the purchase price. The Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China argued that the premises Yutian Company intended to deliver had not passed completion acceptance inspection, and therefore did not meet the statutory conditions for delivery. The court of first instance held that although the law requires that only completed and inspected premises may be delivered for use, the real estate development industry is a pillar industry for economic development. To facilitate economic development, it is common for many large projects to put the podium parts into use after inspection. In this case, the premises Yutian Company intended to deliver to the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China were merely the basement floor of Yutian Building, and this floor had been inspected by the Chongqing Construction Engineering Quality Supervision Station, which affixed its seal of approval on November 7, 2000. Therefore, the "Interim Acceptance Record" for Yutian Building, which was sealed by the Chongqing Construction Engineering Quality Supervision Station on November 7, 2000, can serve as the basis for finding that the premises Yutian Company intended to deliver to the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China met the conditions for delivery. The Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China should pay the first installment of the purchase price in accordance with the agreement. Based on this, the court of first instance held that the "Joint Building Agreement" signed by both parties on March 16, 1996, was valid, the premises Yutian Company intended to deliver met the conditions for delivery, the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China should pay the first installment of the purchase price in accordance with the agreement, and Yutian Company's claim in this regard was supported. Since the Chongqing Construction Engineering Quality Supervision Station affixed its seal on the "Interim Acceptance Record" on November 7, 2000, the time when Yutian Company satisfied the conditions for delivery should be that date. The starting date for calculating any interest or late payment fee payable by the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China should also be the date when the premises met the conditions for delivery. Therefore, Yutian Company's claim for interest and late payment fees for the period from July 30, 1997, to August 2000, had no factual or legal basis and was not supported by the court of first instance. Accordingly, on June 22, 2001, the court rendered Civil Judgment No. 1696 (2000) Yu Yi Zhong Min Chu Zi, holding that: 1. The Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China shall immediately upon the effectiveness of this judgment pay to Yutian Company the first installment of the purchase price in the amount of RMB 29,600,000; 2. All other claims of Yutian Company were dismissed. The court acceptance fee was RMB 221,699.5, and other litigation costs were RMB 1,500, totaling RMB 223,199.5, of which Yutian Company was to bear RMB 74,600 and the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China was to bear RMB 148,599.5 (this amount had been prepaid by Yutian Company and would not be refunded; the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China was to pay it directly to Yutian Company immediately upon the effectiveness of this judgment).

Both Yutian Company and the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China appealed against the first-instance judgment.

The Chongqing High People's Court held at second instance that: 1. The "General Joint Building Agreement" signed by Yutian Company and the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China on January 8, 1996, and the "Joint Building Agreement" signed by the parties on March 16, 1996, were both true expressions of the parties' intent, did not violate legal provisions, and should both be valid contracts. The court of first instance erred in finding that the later agreement amended the earlier one, and therefore only treated the later agreement as the basis for deciding the case. In substance, the later agreement supplemented and perfected the earlier one; both agreements are valid. Because: Yutian Company and the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China signed the "General Joint Building Agreement" on January 8, 1996, stipulating that the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China would invest a total of RMB 57,000,000 in Yutian Company for joint building, and upon completion of the building, it would receive the basement floor shopping area of the building. The basement floor shopping area allocated to the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China was to be accounted for in two parts: one part was funded by the subordinate Business Department of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China with an investment of RMB 20,000,000, receiving 1,000 square meters of the basement floor shopping area; the other part was funded by the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China itself with an investment of RMB 37,000,000, receiving the remaining portion of the basement floor shopping area, including 1,598 square meters of shopping area and 398.53 square meters of common area in the building, with public facilities to be delivered for use within two months after delivery of the premises (the public facilities stipulated in the contract included: A. power supply; B. water supply; C. communication; D. fire protection; E. environmental protection; F. removal and clearance of temporary transitional housing, leveling of sidewalks and landscaping, implementation of lighting projects, etc.; G. other public facilities, etc.). The RMB 37,000,000 was to be paid 80% upon delivery of the premises, 15% upon transfer of title, and the balance upon expiration of the warranty period. The liquidated damages clause provided that if the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China failed to invest according to the agreement, it would pay a late payment fee of 0.1‰ per day of the shortfall; if Yutian Company failed to deliver the premises on time, it would pay a late payment fee of 0.1‰ per day of the total investment amount. Subsequently, in accordance with the agreement, Yutian Company and the Business Department of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China signed a "Joint Building Agreement" on January 20, 1996, and Yutian Company and the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China also signed another "Joint Building Agreement". The latter agreement specified that when the building reached the eighth floor, the Business Department of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China should have fully contributed its investment; it also specified the delivery time and pricing standard for the Business Department's premises: an investment of RMB 20,000,000 to receive 1,000 square meters on the basement floor, with delivery by July 30, 1997, and the Business Department had the right to choose the location within the basement floor. That agreement was fully performed by December 17, 1997. On March 16, 1996, the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China invested a total of RMB 37,000,000 in Yutian Company for joint building, and was to receive 1,996.53 square meters on the basement floor (including 1,598 square meters of shopping area calculated at RMB 21,650 per building square meter, and 398.53 square meters of common area apportionment calculated at RMB 4,500 per square meter). The two "Joint Building Agreements" signed by Yutian Company with the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China and its Business Department, respectively, supplemented and perfected the "General Joint Building Agreement" and should both be deemed valid. The first-instance judgment, which found that the "Joint Building Agreement" amended the "General Joint Building Agreement" and only recognized the later agreement as valid, was incorrect. Accordingly, Yutian Company's grounds of appeal should be supported.

2. The issue of whether the two agreements constitute joint building or real estate purchase. Examining the content of the agreements, the method of allocating premises differs from typical joint building arrangements, where the allocation is directly based on axes or floors. The allocation method agreed upon by the parties here involved calculating the price of the allocated area at RMB 21,650 per square meter, plus a method for settling common area apportionment at RMB 4,500 per square meter. The payment of the investment was not due upon signing the contract, but rather upon Yutian Company's completion of the building and delivery as stipulated in the contract, at which time the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China would pay the first installment of the investment, i.e., 80% of RMB 37,000,000. Yutian Company was responsible for handling the property rights formalities for the delivered premises, and the transfer of title was made a condition for the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China to pay the second installment of the investment. From the above content, this agreement fully resembles the external characteristics of a purchase contract. From the perspective of actual performance, the Business Department of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China had already performed part of the general agreement and had swapped the premises to another floor. As to whether the agreement violated laws and regulations, although at the time Yutian Company signed the agreement with the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, it had not yet obtained the State-owned Land Use Certificate and the Commercial Housing Pre-sale (Pre-lease) Permit for Yutian Building, Yutian Company later obtained both documents. Pursuant to Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (I) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 51 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, this agreement shall be deemed valid. Although both parties engaged in conduct to circumvent the law, this did not cause loss to the State and does not affect the validity of the contract. The claim of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China that the joint building agreement should be invalid for failure to go through joint building procedures is not tenable. The first-instance judgment correctly found that the agreement was in name a joint building but in substance a purchase. The Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China's ground of appeal that the contract violated legal provisions cannot be sustained.

3. The standard for determining whether the premises Yutian Company intended to deliver met the conditions for delivery. The court of first instance erred in finding that the delivery condition was met by the inspection and seal of approval of the Chongqing Construction Engineering Quality Supervision Station on November 7, 2000, and using that date as the time for the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China to pay the first installment of the purchase price. Because: (1) According to the "General Joint Building Agreement" and the two "Joint Building Agreements" signed by the parties, Article 3(4) on Project Standards concerning public facilities stipulated that public facilities were to be delivered for use within two months after delivery of the premises. The public facilities were explicitly divided into seven categories to be completed within two months after delivery (the seven categories were: 1. power supply; 2. water supply; 3. communication; 4. fire protection; 5. environmental protection; 6. removal and clearance of temporary transitional housing, leveling of sidewalks and landscaping, lighting projects; 7. other public facilities). At the time of delivery, the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China was to pay 80% of the price. The contract did not stipulate that a comprehensive evaluation by the Quality Supervision Station was a condition for delivery. (2) Construction of Yutian Building commenced on December 26, 1995. On December 7, 1996, and April 17, 1997, the structural works of the building were inspected by the construction contractor, the design unit, and the Quality Supervision Station, with signatures of acceptance. On October 28, 1997, an inspection and handover was conducted for the -4.45 level, the basement floor, and the fire control center, with an inspection handover opinion stating: inspection passed, suitable for use, handover to the next process of fine decoration approved. This was signed and acknowledged by the Quality Supervision Station, which again affixed its seal on November 8, 2000, as further confirmation. Therefore, as of October 28, 1997, the premises already met the conditions for delivery, rather than the date November 7, 2000, as determined by the original judgment, when the Quality Supervision Station again affixed its seal as proof before deeming the premises to meet delivery conditions. (3) The Business Department of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China affixed its seal on the Handover and Use Verification Form on December 17, 1997, confirming that the premises met the delivery conditions and accepting 1,000 square meters of the premises (this portion did not include common area apportionment). Under the same conditions, the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China had no reason to refuse to accept the premises. The actual delivery date should be December 17, 1997. The Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China's ground of appeal that Yutian Company delayed delivery by more than three years cannot be sustained.

4. The issue of liability for breach of contract by Yutian Company and the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China. According to the parties' contract, Yutian Company was to deliver the basement floor to the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China and its Business Department by July 30, 1997. In fact, after the basement floor of Yutian Building passed inspection on October 28, 1997, Yutian Company handed over the basement floor to the Business Department of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China on December 17, 1997. Yutian Company failed to deliver the premises as agreed and shall bear liability for delayed delivery in accordance with the contract, paying a late fee of 0.1‰ per day of the total investment amount from July 31, 1997, to December 16, 1997. Under the delivery conditions set forth in the contract, the premises passed inspection on October 28, 1997, meeting the delivery conditions. On December 17, 1997, the Business Department of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China accepted 1,000 square meters on the basement floor and paid RMB 20,000,000. At that time, the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China knew that the premises met the contractual delivery conditions but intentionally refused to accept the premises, leaving them vacant for many years and causing expanded losses. The Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China shall bear primary liability. The conduct of the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China constituted a breach of contract. Since the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China failed to make the investment on time, it shall also bear liability for breach of contract in accordance with the parties' agreement, paying a late fee of 0.1‰ per day of the shortfall and interest on the unpaid funds from December 17, 1997, until payment is made. The entire basement floor was purchased by the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China and its Business Department, so there is no issue of division.

In summary, the "General Joint Building Agreement" and the "Joint Building Agreement" signed by Yutian Company and the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China mutually supplement and perfect each other and are both valid. The original trial correctly found the purchase contract valid and correctly ordered the Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China to pay the purchase price. Yutian Company failed to deliver the premises by the agreed time of July 30, 1997, delaying actual delivery until December 17, 1997, and shall bear certain liability. The Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, knowing that the premises met the delivery conditions, intentionally refused to accept the premises and failed to pay, causing expanded losses, and shall bear primary liability. The original judgment did not base its decision on the contractual delivery conditions, payment methods, and time, but instead improperly set November 7, 2000, as the basis for delivery. The Chongqing Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China's claim for late payment fees for delayed delivery shall be supported. Yutian Company's claim for late payment fees and interest on unpaid funds shall also be supported. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, items (1) and (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 85, 111, and 112 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, on November 26, 2001, the court rendered Civil Judgment No. 118 (2001) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi, holding that: 1. Item (1) of Civil Judgment No. 1696 (2000) Yu Yi Zhong Min Chu Zi of the First Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing was affirmed; 2. Item (2) of Civil Judgment No. 1696 (2000) Yu Yi Zhong Min Chu Zi of the First Intermediate People's Court of Chongqing was reversed; 3. Chongqing Yutian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall pay to the Chongqing Branch of Agricultural Bank of China late payment fees calculated at 0.1‰ per day of the total investment amount (RMB 36,000,000) from July 31, 1997, to December 16, 1997; 4. The Chongqing Branch of Agricultural Bank of China shall pay late payment fees on the amount of RMB 29,600,000 as agreed, calculated at 0.1‰ per day from December 17, 1997, until payment is made; 5. The Chongqing Branch of Agricultural Bank of China shall pay interest on the amount of RMB 29,600,000, calculated in installments at the corresponding loan interest rate of the Agricultural Bank of China for the same period from December 17, 1997, until payment is made. The first-instance court acceptance fee was RMB 221,699.5, and other litigation costs were RMB 1,500, totaling RMB 223,199.5, of which Chongqing Yutian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. was to bear RMB 74,600, and the Chongqing Branch of Agricultural Bank of China was to bear RMB 148,599.5; the second-instance court acceptance fee was RMB 221,699.5, and other litigation costs were RMB 1,500, totaling RMB 223,199.5, of which Chongqing Yutian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. was to bear RMB 74,600, and the Chongqing Branch of Agricultural Bank of China was to bear RMB 148,599.5.

The Supreme People's Procuratorate protested, arguing that: the basic facts found by the second-instance judgment in this case lacked evidentiary support and the application of law was erroneous. (1) The second-instance judgment's finding that the Yutian Building was ready for delivery after the intermediate acceptance inspection, and its use of the time when the Agricultural Bank of China (ABC) Chongqing Branch Business Department took possession of the property as the time when ABC Chongqing Branch should have taken possession, lacked evidentiary support and misapplied the law. First, the second-instance judgment's treatment of the 'Intermediate Acceptance Record' for the Yutian Building under construction as evidence of readiness for delivery constituted an erroneous application of law. Second, the second-instance judgment's reliance on the date recorded in the 'Intermediate Acceptance Record' as the time when the Yutian Building met the conditions for delivery and use lacked evidentiary support. Third, the second-instance judgment's inference, based on the fact that another property buyer, the ABC Chongqing Branch Business Department, took possession of the property on December 17, 1997, that ABC Chongqing Branch should also have taken possession under the same conditions at that time, or else be in breach of contract, lacked evidentiary support. (2) The second-instance judgment's order that ABC Chongqing Branch pay interest on RMB 29.6 million (the down payment stipulated in the contract) lacked factual and legal basis. First, the second-instance judgment's finding that 'the Joint Building Agreement signed by Yutian Company and ABC Chongqing Branch on March 16, 1996, was a supplement and perfection of the Joint Building General Agreement signed on January 8, 1996' contravened the true intent of the parties. Second, the second-instance judgment's order that 'ABC Chongqing Branch pay interest on RMB 29.6 million (the down payment stipulated in the contract)' lacked factual and legal basis.

ABC Chongqing Branch stated in its petition for retrial: The second-instance judgment's ruling on ABC Chongqing Branch's liability for breach of contract exceeded Yutian Company's claims and appellate requests, violating the principle of 'no trial without complaint'. In its appellate brief, Yutian Company only claimed interest, not liquidated damages. At the same time, in its statement of claim, it sought interest from July 30, 1997 to August 2000, but in its appellate brief, it changed the time period for calculating interest to November 1997 to July 2001, thereby increasing the claim for interest. The second-instance court failed to review and adjudicate Yutian Company's waiver of the claim for liquidated damages on appeal and its increase of the claim for interest; instead it further ordered ABC Chongqing Branch to bear interest and liquidated damages until the date of payment, which exceeded Yutian Company's claims. It otherwise agreed with the procuratorate's protest opinions. It requested the reversal of items 4 and 5 of the second-instance judgment.

Yutian Company replied in its defense: First, where the Joint Building Agreement signed after the Joint Building General Agreement is inconsistent with the general agreement on the same subject matter, the later agreement, being the supplement and perfection, should prevail, which is in accordance with legal provisions. Second, the conditions for ABC Chongqing Branch to pay the initial installment of the purchase price to Yutian Company had been fulfilled. According to the Joint Building Agreement, when the subordinate Business Department of ABC Chongqing Branch made the first selection of the property, Yutian Company had already allocated the property to ABC Chongqing Branch, but ABC Chongqing Branch did not pay the initial installment as agreed. Based on the fulfillment of the conditions for property allocation stipulated in the agreement, Yutian Company filed suit alleging breach of contract by ABC Chongqing Branch and sought payment of the initial installment plus liquidated damages and interest. The original judgment ordering ABC Chongqing Branch to pay the initial installment of RMB 29.6 million plus liquidated damages and interest from December 17, 1997 until the date of payment was correct. It requested that ABC Chongqing Branch's claims be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

The Court upon retrial holds: The original judgment's finding that the contents of the Joint Building General Agreement and the Joint Building Agreement represented the true intent of the parties, did not violate the law, and were valid and legally binding, is correct. At the time of this retrial, the parties, ABC Chongqing Branch and Yutian Company, did not raise any objections to the nature, validity, or the issue of paying the initial installment of the purchase price under the signed Joint Building General Agreement and Joint Building Agreement, and these issues did not involve harm to national or other persons' interests. Therefore, the above matters are not within the scope of this retrial. Based on the protest opinions of the procuratorial authority and the arguments of the parties, the main issues in dispute in this case can be summarized as follows: First, whether the Yutian Building was ready for delivery after the intermediate acceptance inspection, and the time and basis for ABC Chongqing Branch's obligation to take possession. Second, the basis for the order that ABC Chongqing Branch pay interest on RMB 29.6 million. Third, whether the original judgment's ruling on ABC Chongqing Branch's liability for breach of contract exceeded Yutian Company's claims.

I. Regarding whether the Yutian Building was ready for delivery after the intermediate acceptance inspection, and the time and basis for ABC Chongqing Branch's obligation to take possession.

1. Concerning whether the Yutian Building was ready for delivery after the intermediate acceptance inspection. Regardless of whether the legal relationship formed between Yutian Company and ABC Chongqing Branch under the Joint Building General Agreement and the Joint Building Agreement is characterized as a joint building relationship or a real estate sales contract relationship, the contents agreed upon in the Joint Building General Agreement and the Joint Building Agreement represented the true intent of the parties, did not violate the law, and are valid and binding contracts that must be strictly performed. Article 5 of the Joint Building General Agreement, regarding the transfer of the building, stipulates: Yutian Company shall, by July 1997, ensure the completion of the public facilities specified in Article 3, Paragraph 4, and then deliver the building to ABC Chongqing Branch for its fine decoration, and Yutian Company shall cooperate. ABC Chongqing Branch's decoration must not damage the structure, public facilities, or common areas, and during the decoration period, it must comply with Yutian Company's overall arrangements. From this, it can be determined that the condition for delivery agreed by the parties was for Yutian Company to deliver the building to ABC Chongqing Branch for fine decoration after completing the public facilities stipulated in the contract. The Joint Building General Agreement and the Joint Building Agreement, under the engineering standards, specify that the public facilities consist of seven parts: power supply, water supply, communication, fire protection, environmental protection, removal and clearance of temporary transitional housing, leveling of sidewalks and landscaping, lighting projects, and other public facilities. Construction of the Yutian Building commenced on December 26, 1995. The structural works of the building were accepted by the construction unit, design unit, and quality supervision station on December 7, 1996 and April 17, 1997. The parties did not raise any objections regarding the completion of the public facilities. Furthermore, the quality supervision station, design unit, builder (or supervisor), and construction unit accepted the structural works of the Yutian Building. The quality supervision station, design unit, receiving party, and transferring party accepted the -4.45 level and basement level 1 of the building, explicitly confirming that the acceptance was qualified, that the building met the conditions for use, and that it was approved for transfer to the next process of fine decoration. ABC Chongqing Branch did not dispute that the 'Intermediate Acceptance Record' was intended for transfer to the next process. In summary, after the intermediate acceptance inspection, the Yutian Building met the conditions agreed upon by the parties for the transfer of the building. The original judgment's finding that the Yutian Building was ready for delivery after the intermediate acceptance inspection was not improper. However, the original judgment's reasoning that the contract did not require a comprehensive assessment by the municipal quality supervision station as a condition for delivery was inappropriate. ABC Chongqing Branch's argument that the original judgment's treatment of the 'Intermediate Acceptance Record' for the Yutian Building under construction as evidence of readiness for delivery constituted an erroneous application of law cannot be sustained, and this Court does not support it.

2. Concerning the time and basis for ABC Chongqing Branch's obligation to take possession. The inspection and transfer opinions in the 'Intermediate Acceptance Record' can only serve as evidence that the conditions agreed upon by the parties for the transfer of the building were met; the date recorded therein cannot be determined as the time of delivery and use of the building. Because meeting the conditions for delivery does not necessarily mean that Yutian Company immediately delivered the building to ABC Chongqing Branch. Yutian Company failed to provide evidence proving that it notified ABC Chongqing Branch to take possession on December 17, 1997. Therefore, the original judgment's inference, based on the fact that the ABC Chongqing Branch Business Department took possession of the property on December 17, 1997, that ABC Chongqing Branch should also have taken possession under the same conditions at that time, and its use of December 17, 1997 as the date by which ABC Chongqing Branch should have taken possession, was incorrect. The grounds for ABC Chongqing Branch's petition are valid, and this Court supports them. The existing evidence shows that Yutian Company first notified ABC Chongqing Branch to take possession of the building on October 19, 1998. ABC Chongqing Branch did not object to this notice. The time for ABC Chongqing Branch to take possession should be determined based on the content of the letter sent by Yutian Company. Yutian Company required ABC Chongqing Branch to take possession before October 23, 1998, indicating that this date was the deadline for taking possession. Therefore, it can be determined that the date by which ABC Chongqing Branch should have taken possession was October 23, 1998.

II. Regarding the basis for the order that ABC Chongqing Branch pay interest on RMB 29.6 million.

The Joint Building General Agreement and the Joint Building Agreement were agreements reached voluntarily and on an equal footing by the parties, conforming to legal provisions, and are valid and legally binding. The contents stipulated in these two agreements shall impose binding obligations on the parties. Where two contracts (agreements) are both valid, except where the parties have specifically agreed otherwise, if the two contracts (agreements) contain conflicting provisions on the same subject matter, based on the principle that the most recent expression of intent prevails and does not contradict the purpose of the contract (agreement), the content of the later contract (agreement) shall prevail, determined by the chronological order of their formation. If the contents stipulated in the two contracts (agreements) are not in conflict but merely contain different stipulations on the subject matter, it cannot be simply concluded that the later agreement is an amendment of the earlier agreement, or that it is a supplement and perfection of the earlier agreement. Comparing the Joint Building General Agreement with the Joint Building Agreement, it can be seen that the Joint Building Agreement additionally stipulated that ABC Chongqing Branch would acquire 1,996.53 square meters of the basement level 1 of the building calculated on a per-square-meter basis (including 1,598 square meters of commercial space at RMB 21,650 per square meter, and 398.53 square meters of common area apportionment at RMB 4,500 per square meter). It additionally stipulated that Yutian Company should deliver the building to ABC Chongqing Branch for use by July 30, 1997. It did not repeat the provisions regarding 'if ABC Chongqing Branch's investment is not made on time, the resulting interest shall be borne by ABC Chongqing Branch' and 'to ensure the smooth completion of the joint building, ABC Chongqing Branch shall coordinate loans and introduce project construction through multiple channels; interest on such loans shall be calculated according to the prevailing national standards at that time. The amount of coordinated loans and introduced funds shall not be less than the investment amount of the second part' and other related investment content. Therefore, the additions in the Joint Building Agreement, or the absence of repeated stipulations of the relevant content of the Joint Building General Agreement, merely constitute adjustments to the content of the agreement, and there is no conflict between the two. Given that both agreements are valid, their stipulated contents shall bind the parties. ABC Chongqing Branch's argument that the original judgment's finding that the Joint Building Agreement signed by Yutian Company and ABC Chongqing Branch was a supplement and perfection of the Joint Building General Agreement contravened the true intent of the parties cannot be sustained. The provisions in the Joint Building General Agreement and the Joint Building Agreement regarding 'if ABC Chongqing Branch's investment is not made on time, the resulting interest shall be borne by ABC Chongqing Branch' and 'if ABC Chongqing Branch's investment is not made on time, liquidated damages of 0.1‰ of the shortfall per day shall be paid; if Yutian Company fails to deliver the building on time, liquidated damages of 0.1‰ of the total investment amount per day shall be paid' are measures established by the parties to ensure the performance of contractual rights and obligations. Since both the Joint Building General Agreement and the Joint Building Agreement are valid, and ABC Chongqing Branch did not object to the content of the letter sent by Yutian Company on October 19, 1998, which explicitly stated that from October 23, 1998, it would no longer bear the interest on the RMB 37 million purchase price, the original judgment's order that ABC Chongqing Branch pay liquidated damages and then also pay interest on RMB 29.6 million (the down payment stipulated in the contract) does not lack factual and legal basis.

III. Regarding whether the original judgment's ruling on ABC Chongqing Branch's liability for breach of contract exceeded Yutian Company's claims.

The parties' disposition of their civil and procedural rights within the scope provided by law, and the principle of 'no trial without complaint', are important principles in civil litigation. When adjudicating civil and commercial disputes, the people's court can only make a determination on the civil rights and obligations that have been brought before it. Except where national or public interests are involved, its trial and judgment shall be limited to the scope of the parties' requests and claims. The content of the parties' claims includes not only their statements of claim, requests for additional claims, defenses, refutations, and counterclaims in the first instance, but also their appellate requests and appellate defenses in the second instance. It also includes their statements, submission of evidence, arguments, cross-examination, mediation, and any inquiries made by the people's court during the trial. Viewing the overall content of Yutian Company's statement of claim, its appeal, and the second-instance court's inquiry, Yutian Company not only requested in the first instance that ABC Chongqing Branch assume the responsibility of paying the initial installment of the joint building funds of RMB 29.6 million, plus interest and liquidated damages for the delayed payment, but also, during the second-instance court's inquiry, still requested that ABC Chongqing Branch assume the responsibility of paying interest and liquidated damages for the delayed payment, and required that the cut-off point be up to the date of payment. This fully demonstrates that Yutian Company did not waive its rights. Although the specific amounts of Yutian Company's requests for interest and liquidated damages for the delayed payment varied depending on the different cut-off points for calculation at different stages of litigation, and to some extent constituted an increase in the claims, this increase was necessarily incurred due to the extension of the time point. To reduce litigation burden, the original trial court's handling of the matter together based on the parties' claims was not improper. Therefore, the original judgment's ruling on ABC Chongqing Branch's liability for breach of contract did not exceed Yutian Company's claims. ABC Chongqing Branch's argument that the original judgment exceeded Yutian Company's claims cannot be sustained, and this Court does not support it.

In summary, the parties have no objection to the original judgment's ruling on the payment of the initial installment of the purchase price. The handling of that part in the original judgment should be affirmed. Pursuant to the agreement, Yutian Company failed to deliver the building to ABC Chongqing Branch by July 30, 1997, constituting a breach of contract, and it should bear the liability for late delivery in accordance with the agreement. The original judgment's determination of December 17, 1997, the date when the ABC Chongqing Branch Business Department took possession, as the date by which ABC Chongqing Branch should have taken possession lacked sufficient basis. The final date for taking possession as notified by Yutian Company, October 23, 1998, should be used as the cut-off date for its late delivery. The original judgment's order that Yutian Company pay liquidated damages at 0.1‰ of the total investment amount per day from July 31, 1997 to December 16, 1997 was incorrect and should be corrected. Yutian Company notified ABC Chongqing Branch to take possession before October 23, 1998. ABC Chongqing Branch failed to take possession of the building on time and also failed to perform its payment obligations as agreed. Its actions constituted a breach of contract. Pursuant to the agreement, it should bear the liability for breach of contract for interest and liquidated damages on the delayed payment. The time of breach should run from October 23, 1998. The original judgment's use of December 17, 1997 as the starting date was incorrect and should be corrected. Therefore, Civil Judgment (2001) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 118 of the Chongqing High People's Court found some facts unclearly and misapplied the law. Some of the grounds for the parties' petition are valid. Pursuant to Article 186 and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (1), (2), and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. Affirm Items 1 and 2 of Civil Judgment (2001) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 118 of the Chongqing High People's Court;

2. Amend Item 3 of Civil Judgment (2001) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 118 of the Chongqing High People's Court to read: Chongqing Yutian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall pay to Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd. Chongqing Branch liquidated damages on the total investment amount of RMB 37 million at the rate of 0.1‰ per day (from July 31, 1997 to October 23, 1998);

3. Amend Item 4 of Civil Judgment (2001) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 118 of the Chongqing High People's Court to read: Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd. Chongqing Branch shall pay liquidated damages on RMB 29.6 million as agreed, calculated at 0.1‰ per day from October 23, 1998 until the date of payment.

4. Amend Item 5 of Civil Judgment (2001) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 118 of the Chongqing High People's Court to read: Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd. Chongqing Branch shall pay interest on RMB 29.6 million, calculated in installments according to the same period comparable interest rate of Agricultural Bank of China, from October 23, 1998 until the date of payment.

The first and second instance case acceptance fees total RMB 443,393, and other litigation fees total RMB 3,000. The total litigation fees are RMB 446,393, of which Chongqing Yutian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 149,200, and Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd. Chongqing Branch shall bear RMB 297,193.

This judgment is final.
